questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm
questions.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x}={2}^{x+1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x} & ={2}^{x+1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x-1}={3}^{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-1} & ={3}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 & =1 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =1 \\ x & =\frac{1}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x-5}={4}^{x}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-5} & ={4}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-5}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & =5 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm: Advanced Cases
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{4-x} & ={8}^{2x+3} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{4-x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{2x+3})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(4-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)=(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(4-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ -x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x & =\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{4x+1} & ={6}^{7x+5} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{4x+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{7x+5})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(4x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)=(7x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(4x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(7x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =7x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x & =\frac{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}\end{aligned}
$$
